_about: Single source of cross-feature known risks for the « Éditeur de livre dont vous êtes le héros ». Aggregated from every features/*/specification.json plus the global engineering rules in SKILL.md/CLAUDE.md. Banded ids: 0xx = per-feature domain risks (stable, gaps expected); 1xx = global cross-cutting engineering rules. Ids are stable references — never renumber; append new ones at the next free id within the right band.

known_risks.risk: Seed must be atomic and EXACT: a book always contains exactly Sommaire + isolated Mort. Seed through one BookService factory, never ad hoc.
The Mort node is isolated by contract (0 edges) and obligatory; it is locked (not deletable/duplicable, type fixed, only text editable) and never auto-linked on create.
Book id is collision-free and stable; the id, not the title, is the persistence key. Ids via brain/utils/id. All references (objects, monsters, node targets) are by stable id, never by name.

Navigation and events fire only AFTER persistence resolves, in order (e.g. book:created -> book:opened). Listeners must always observe a persisted book. Any callback that closes over mutable state needs a stable ref.
No raw window.localStorage in feature files; persist only via PersistenceService and the key builders in persistenceKeys.ts. Feature-level facet of global KR-111.
No useEffect for derived state — compute inline or with useMemo. Legitimate useEffect: subscriptions, imperative DOM/third-party APIs, external-store syncing. Feature-level facet of global KR-113.

The canvas is a VIEW, not the model: never mutate node/edge data locally; all changes go through BookService so outline-view and game-preview stay consistent. Local-only edits desync the visualizations.
Orphaned edges (source/target node deleted) must be dropped or visibly flagged, never rendered as a line to nowhere or a crash. Reconcile on every render / node:deleted.

Pan/zoom and canvas<->outline view-mode are UI preferences (UIPreferencesService), explicitly NOT part of the synced book document; pushing them to CloudSyncService causes spurious conflicts (cloud-first boundary).
Node positions belong to the book document and must persist; position-less nodes use a deterministic layout (no random scatter, no 0,0 pileup) so reopening a book is stable.

Node selection is the single source of truth in the brain SelectionService (promoted from tree-canvas local state). Canvas and node-editor both read via useSelectedNode and write via selection.select; the service is the sole emitter of node:selected and clears on book:opened. No feature keeps a competing copy (avoids two-panel desync).

node-editor is a HOST shell: the action body (PNJ/décor/piège/monstre) and the choices list are mounted from other features via ActionRegistry / feature slots. Importing an action feature directly would break feature isolation.

Adding a new action type must require ZERO changes to node-editor: the SegmentedControl options + the mounted editor come from the ActionRegistry. Hard-coding a type couples node-editor to a specialty (Open/Closed).
Objects carry a player-facing DESCRIPTION, not just a name; the inventory editor must capture both via the shared brain ObjectEditor, never a bare string (domain rule).

Selection swap must not leak the previous node's uncommitted field state into the next node. Bind fields to the store (no local mirror) and/or key the panel subtree by node id so it resets on selection change.

Turning a node into a Fin (victoire/échec) changes its kind/badge everywhere; the end flags live on the node in BookService and the FIN badge is derived (effectiveKind/endLabel) so canvas/outline/panel reflect it from one source via node:updated.

Sommaire (root) and Mort (death leaf) are STRUCTURAL screens: no « libellé du choix », no « action requise pour poursuivre », no Fin victoire/échec toggles. Mort additionally has NO outgoing choices. Their only editable field is the text. Enforce both in the UI (hide those sections) AND in BookService.updateNode (text-only patch for sommaire/mort), so the invariant holds at the SSOT, not just the panel.

Edges are the book's structure: all create/delete goes through BookService (addChoiceBranch/addEdge/removeEdge) so tree-canvas + outline-view + game-preview agree; never mutate edges locally (re-asserts KR-020). Mort may not have outgoing edges — enforced at the SSOT, not just the UI (KR-055).

Relink allows cycles/convergence by DESIGN but must guard degenerate cases: no duplicate identical edges, sane self-link handling, and the target node is never created/deleted by relinking (only the edge). [self-link/duplicate guards land in iteration 2]
Hidden prerequisite references an object by STABLE id from ObjectCatalogService, not by name; a dangling reference to a deleted object must be detected, not silently treated as true/false.

Countdown fallback + relink targets are node references that can dangle if the target is deleted; run a referential-integrity check and surface broken targets rather than crashing the reader later (re-asserts KR-021).
Deleting a `choice` branch may orphan its child subtree; prompt/handle explicitly — do not silently leave unreachable nodes or cascade-delete without consent.
A choice may hold BOTH a hidden prerequisite and a countdown; the countdown only ticks while the choice is visible (prerequisite met), so a hidden choice never expires invisibly.

Cross-feature panel composition uses the brain SlotRegistry: a host (node-editor) reserves a slot id (SLOT_NODE_EDITOR_CHOICES) and renders whatever is registered, falling back to a placeholder; a provider (choice-linking) registers a renderer at the composition root (App). Neither feature imports the other — same OCP seam as ActionRegistry, for arbitrary panel regions.

Structural screens are never authored choice targets: the Sommaire root has no incoming choices and the Mort leaf is reached ONLY automatically at the end of a combat, never via a choice/relink. Enforce at the SSOT (BookService.addEdge rejects a target whose kind is sommaire/mort) AND in the relink picker (exclude them from candidates), not just one. The future automatic combat→Mort link uses a dedicated path, not the manual edge API.

Per-kind knowledge lives in ONE data-driven registry (brain/kinds.ts: NODE_KINDS / EDGE_KINDS), not scattered if (kind === …) tests or partial maps. Each descriptor carries the kind's label, default title, badge mark, and domain invariants (structural / canHaveOutgoing / canBeTarget). Consumers (NodeBadge, nodeView, effectiveKind, NodeEditorPanel, BookService, EdgeLayer, OutgoingChoices) READ the descriptor. The registry is the SINGLE source even for the NodeKind/EdgeKind union types: each is derived with `keyof typeof` via the `defineKinds` factory, which infers the key union while pinning every entry to the descriptor shape — so there is no separate union to keep in sync, a missing descriptor field fails to compile, and there is no silent Partial<Record> gap. Kinds stay plain string literals (JSON-serialised domain) — descriptors, not classes, are the 'replace conditional with polymorphism' answer here. Same Open/Closed seam as ActionRegistry (KR-051).

Deleting a book is a dangerous, irreversible action: always gate behind a confirmation dialog (name the book, error-toned confirm, labelled Annuler) and route the delete through BookService.deleteBook (persist-remove then book:deleted, KR-004) — never a raw removal.

The library list is a VIEW over BookService via useBooks (recomputed only on book:created/book:deleted, cached snapshot for useSyncExternalStore), never a private copy (re-asserts KR-020/013). Deleting the currently-open book could leave the editor on a dangling route — guard it (navigate home) when that path exists. [guard lands in iteration 2]

book-creation and book-library compose at the app root: LibraryScreen receives the create affordance as a prop (<CreateBookEntry/>); neither feature imports the other (feature isolation). Same composition-root seam as the ActionRegistry/SlotRegistry, for a sibling screen rather than a panel region.

Any presentational component consumed by more than one feature belongs in brain/components/ and is re-exported from brain/components/index.ts. A component living in a feature but imported by another is a cross-feature violation — move it.
Any utility used by more than one feature belongs in brain/utils/, never in a feature's own utils/. Importing from a sibling feature's utils/ is a cross-feature violation.

No raw window.localStorage in feature files — use PersistenceService for the book document and useUIPreferences()/UIPreferencesService (via brain/) for non-synced UI state. Single auditable storage surface.
Component/hook size limits: a file over 400 lines is a split signal (extract subcomponents/hooks); a file over 800 lines is a merge blocker.
No useEffect-synced mirrors of props/derived state; never use // eslint-disable react-hooks/exhaustive-deps to mask a stale closure — fix the root cause (stable refs, recompute inline).

Any localStorage key holding a credential/token/secret (PAT, OAuth, API key) must be registered in brain/persistenceKeys.ts with a /* SENSITIVE */ marker and annotated in UIPreferenceKey — one auditable location for all credential storage. None yet.

A design value needed both as a CSS string and as a numeric JS value lives in TWO synced forms: a CSS token (e.g. --hit-target: 44px in styles/tokens) and a mirrored brain constant (e.g. HIT_TARGET_MIN = 44 in brain/ui.ts). Use the token in CSS/style strings and the constant only where a number is required (numeric size props). The two MUST stay in sync — never reintroduce the bare literal at call sites.
